Sabrent SB-256-EC-NVME-BLK 256Gb NVMe USB 3.1 External Aluminum SSD The Sabrent External SSD honestly saved my day. My MacBook Pro’s display developed funky lines out of the blue, so it had to go in for a hardware repair. I write and save everything on my hard drive, so naturally I wanted a ton of backups. Just in case the worst happened and I ended up losing everything during the repair.

My appointment was set up for the next day, so I had little time to make a ton of backups. AND there was a massive thunderstorm, so the power kept flickering. I tried a normal stick first, and the estimated time was like 3 HOURS to copy everything. I so didn’t have time for that. I plugged the Sabrent in, started the copy, and went to get a drink. When I came back in less than five minutes, it was finished!!

I just now copied a 16gb folder in 48.15 seconds.

The USB-C adapter on the cord is also very handy, if you use the Sabrent on several computers or other devices. When I use the Sabrent on my MacBook Pro, I’m unable to plug anything else into the neighboring USB port because the adapter is blocky. But I’ll take the convenience of having one on the cord rather than having to go hunt for an adapter in my office.

The SSD itself is quite small. Very portable. The box the SSD comes in is great for storing the drive between uses, too. There’s a slightly padded interior compartment and a spot for the cord.
text_fidelity_b: Sabrent SB-256-EC-NVME-BLK 256Gb NVMe USB 3.1 External Aluminum SSD

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D810 FX-format Digital SLR Camera Body I have had this camera since July 2015 and I find that this camera to be the most incredible camera I have ever owned. I have owned the D700, D800, D600, D610 and still own the D750.The clarity and dynamic range surpasses all of my previous cameras, including my D750.
However, the D810 is very demanding on lenses. Inferior lenses will provide either inconsistent performance, or just plain horrendous results.
Edit: 11/29/2017: After over two years of regular use I have had no problems with this camera. I have never had to clean my sensor, and I change lenses frequently, as I most often use prime lenses. So, I don’t understand why so many people have the need to frequently to “dust off” or clean their sensor. Nor do I understand why some people complain about the fact that most of the outer shell is made of carbon fiber. For years I worked with advanced composites, and carbon fiber is not just cheap plastic, but is used in many high-tech products for its superior strength and light weight.
I can only speak from my own experience and knowledge.

text_fidelity_a:
USB Power Strip Tower, BESFAN Surge Protector with 12 Outlets and 5 USB Ports, 10ft Extension Cord USB (Desktop Smart Charging Station) for Home, Dorm and Office As most of us know – if we have electronics (laptops, iPads, phones) – we need a surge protector.

And, since about 2003 – I’ve had TONS of them. Even ones that protected the landline cord (do we even have landlines anymore). I’ve had wide/flat, narrow/flat, and just ones that mounted to a wall.

I’ve had ones that didn’t have enough outlets either, or the outlets were spaced just “so” that I couldn’t plug up adapter type plugs (phones, etc). And, ones that the wall cord was so short they didn’t help out much in certain areas.

This one?

WOW! Game changer!

Not only the shape – I would never have thought of a tower design. But, it does save room. I have mine under my desk and with my old flat one – I ended up turning it off countless times. Not this one though. Outlets? 12 outlets which comes in handy, along with five (5) USB ports.

This is a LONG wall cord so plugging it into outlets further/farther away than where you need it is not a huge problem. Unless the outlet is across the room.

The outlets on this unit are spaced and sectioned for big or small plugs. And, the USB ports are a huge bonus! Some devices don’t come with a wall adapter and either you spend money on one, or you have to hook it up to your computer. This? That eliminates that situation.

I can’t attest to others’ and their phones – this charges my phone in the same amount of time as the wall adapter to the USB cord would. So, not much difference there.

Other than the cool stuff, this functions just like other surge protectors. No issues so far. It’s fairly sturdy and I’m definitely glad I got this! I’m definitely sold on this design and I plan to upgrade my household with them as I can.

I definitely wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this. Would make a great “house-warming” gift.
text_fidelity_b: USB Power Strip Tower, BESFAN Surge Protector with 12 Outlets and 5 USB Ports, 10ft Extension Cord USB (Desktop Smart Charging Station) for Home, Dorm and Office

Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack GMRS walkie-talkies like this have been around for decades. Unfortunately, the technology hasn't really improved in all that time. The specs that are listed in the description are greatly exaggerated. We only get 4-5 hours of moderate use from the rechargeable batteries. Fortunately, you can replace them with fresh AA batteries in the field to extend your usage time. The 20 mile range is really a hoax. Even the most optimal situation when one of us is on top of a hill and the others are visible in the valley below, we've never gotten more than 10 miles. In clear flat situations like across a lake or a farm field, range is a 3-4 miles at best. In a forest or city where there are lots of obstructions, range can be less than 1 mile.

20 years ago, few people had cell phones so these radios were really popular. Not so much anymore. That means you get much less interference on each channel. We find the radios useful for family outings since the kids don't have cell phones and many of the parks we visit have terrible cell phone coverage.

The radios are fairly lightweight (about 6 ounces each including the batteries). The package includes 3 battery packs and 2 chargers. One of the chargers has a splitter so it can charge 2 radios at the same time. You can also use your micro-USB cell phone charger to charge the radios. You can also use your own rechargeable AA batteries with your own charger. Replacing the batteries is kind of a hassle since the belt clip blocks the battery cover, though I suppose that also helps keep the battery cover in place. No carrying cases or storage case is included, through the radios are pretty durable and the shipping box works well for storage.

Note that USA use requires a Federal FCC radio license. The photo here is from the instruction manual. Many (perhaps most) users violate Federal law and use them without license, but who knows what enforcement will be like in the future. Other countries have stricter laws and I have heard about some tourists getting into trouble using radios like this.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA) I got my first PC in 2003, and had a corded mouse. Looking back, I can BARELY remember the mouse that came with that Gateway PC. In 2004, my mom bought a Dell PC and traded me for my Gateway – don’t judge, she just wanted something to browse the internet and play games on.

Between 2003-2005, I used an awkward racecar shaped mouse, but went back to the more streamlined corded mouse for my desktops.

In 2005, when I got a laptop, I got my first wireless mouse and liked it. It was a Logitech.

By 2010, I got my first HP laptop – and as usual, got a specific mouse for it, again Logitech. The reason? My hand. I don’t have very big hands and hate to “splay” my fingers out trying to grip the mouse. That continued with a backup laptop in 2011 with some college money.

I even got “backup” mice, I just LOVED the Logitech ones.

Last year, 2021, I got another HP laptop for my birthday and yes – a “Logi” mouse (M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top). This was a bit smaller than my previous mice. But, I love it.

Thinking this might be a bit better – I got it.

Right off – it is a bit “extra”. I can BARELY grip it to get it to do what I need to do. The “thumb” rest was a good idea, the USB rechargeable feature was nice, programmable buttons – a bit beyond me. This is definitely for someone who needs those features.

As far as “quiet” with regards to the scrolling and clicking – I don’t see the need for the feature. When I’m typing on they keyboard that is noisier than my mouse.

It was response and fast – but not enough to justify a purchase of it.

It connects the same way my “Logi” does – USB dongle. Both mice take ONE (1) AA battery

At the current price of $67.52 – this is a definitely no-go for me.
text_fidelity_b: HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA)

TP-Link Wireless N300 PCI Adapter, 2.4GHz 300Mbps -(TL-WN851ND) While there isn't as great a NEED for this as there used to be, as so many devices have built in wireless, when you have a tower that needs it, this is the answer.
Basically, because of even the higher demands (Skype, streaming, etc) you need that strong signal without drops, both ways. This has a feature called MIMO, which instead of the standard adapter that has one antenna for reception, THIS has multiple antennae to accommodate 2 ways, and to reduce drops in data.
Be sure you disable the anti-virus, failure to do so and it just doesn't work. If you periodically lose the signal and require a reboot, then uninstall the driver in utility, and install the driver only. Then use Windows embedded wireless utility to connect to your wireless network.

Go to the manufacturer site for some excellent recommendations, like if there's a reduction in signal after a few months, set the router to a static channel (like 1, 3, 6, or 9).
For the money, this seems to be a pretty good product, at least in my case.
I've had very good experiences this company's products, as well as customer service.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Wireless N300 PCI Adapter, 2.4GHz 300Mbps -(TL-WN851ND)

text_fidelity_a:
AMD FD8350FRHKBOX FX-8350 FX-Series 8-Core Black Edition Processor Immediately after installing I noticed the idle speed just sitting in BIOS to be 50C. That's quite a bit! More than any processor I've come across.
At first I thought I seated it wrong so I undid the heat sink, used really good thermal paste and tried once more.
Same result. Idle temp at 50C.
And under load it's getting up to into the low 60s and termal throttling like crazy. However it seems to perform well even under that heavy load, which is nice if that's all you care about.
But I'm doing a build for my dad and I don't think he'd be content with having to hear a jet engine under his desk day in and day out. So I'm going to have to look elsewhere.
That's on me though. I probably should have known better from my experience with another FX processor. Ah well.
Still considering if I'm returning this or not.

UPDATE:
Ok, I did some more digging and it sounds like my motherboard is not equipped to handle this processor.
WARNING: If you have a MSI 970A-G46 Motherboard DO NOT BUY THIS PROCESSOR.
Go research "MSI 970A-G46 FX 8350"
You'll find numerous testimonials of people who have had terminal issues trying to use a FX 8350 with this board.
Since the MB is at fault for this and I can not accurately benchmark this product, I'll give AMD the benefit of the doubt and make this 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: AMD FD8350FRHKBOX FX-8350 FX-Series 8-Core Black Edition Processor

Canvas Laptop Backpack Shoulder Bag - College Outdoor - Fit 15" Laptop (Brown) I’m really impressed with this backpack. Given the price point, I was expecting a so-so pack with limited functionality. Instead, this backpack has quite a few well-done features, and the overall appearance is very striking.

It’s made mostly of canvas, which gives is a “broken in” look right from the start. It’s a very nice change from the usual nylon packs. The canvas is thick and sturdy, and has a great feel to it.

The build quality is impressive considering the price. The stitching is all tight and even, the zippers are of good quality, and the snaps/fasteners are all solid and durable. The strap padding is a little thin, but still comfortable. I was really pleased to see that there was padding on the back. That’s not an option I was expecting at this price. It gives the pack a much more comfortable feel when it’s loaded down.

The inside is lined with a smooth, snag-free lining that’s either nylon or poly (not 100% sure). In any case, it is also very well stitched, with no loose threads, sags or puckers in the material. It makes it very easy to slide books, laptops, etc. in and out of the pack. There are also a couple of compartments inside the pack, both zippered and open, to help organize all the little items that everyone needs to tote around. Additional pouches are on the outside of the pack, which are great for easy access. I didn't have any problem stowing all my small items inside of some type of pouch.

The size is ample for a typical laptop plus a few other items. I loaded it down with books to see if it could take the weight, and the pack performed very well.

The build quality, looks and performance make this an excellent value for the price. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a pack that won’t break the bank in terms of cost.
[Sample provided for review]

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMC-TS6A LUMIX WiFi Enabled Tough Adventure Camera (Blue) I’m a big fan of the Panasonic Lumix line of point and shoot cameras. I’ve been using one for years and, while it has limited features by today’s standards, it has yet to let me down. This latest one in the Lumix line offers a huge range of capabilities, provides outstanding image quality, but continues to suffer from a less than ideal user interface.

The camera comes with just the basics: the camera, a single battery, lanyard and a charger (plus manuals and software). I was a little disappointed right off the bat when I saw the charger. Unlike the older Lumix chargers that had a wall plug built into the charger than flipped out, this has a separate power cord. While that does make it easier to plug into the wall, it also means I have to remember to carry the cord with me to charge it.

Initial setup is straightforward, with the usual time/date setting. Since this has a GPS there’s also the need to go through initializing that option as well. All of these steps can be skipped, but you’ll be reminded to do so every time you power on the camera. It also displays a warning on screen about the waterproof limitations of the camera (and provides ample documentation as to what it can/can’t do re: underwater use).

The view screen is wonderful. Sharp, clear, and easy to read in all lightning conditions. The menu system will be familiar if you’ve ever used a Lumix camera but, if not, it’s still pretty straightforward. I still think Canon has the lead when it comes to having an intuitive point and shoot menu system, but Panasonic does a decent job. I like that with most options there’s a scrolling line of text that comes up to explain what the option is/does. That’s very helpful for options you don’t often use and need help with, but it does not interfere or slow down operation should you know exactly what you want to select.

I won’t list all the camera specs in this review since those are easily available in the listing and the Panasonic web site. Suffice it to say this offers a huge range of options and capabilities that cover pretty much any shooting situation. The Intelligent mode shooting scenario options (of which there are many) are helpful when you just want to point the camera and have it do everything else for you, including compensation for specialized lighting/scene situations. I especially like the macro option, which produced some impressive close-up shots that were sharply focused and clear even though I didn’t use a table-top tripod for stability but relied on the image stabilization features of the camera.

The video recording image quality is excellent good for a point and shoot cam. The performance of the built in mic is decent as well. This won’t compete with a dedicated HD cam, but for casual video shooting it’s a small, simple and easy to use setup that gets the job done pretty well.

The WiFi setup was surprisingly easy. I was dreading that since it often can be a bear, but this was quick and easy, and the included instructions were easy to follow. I use the WiFi option a lot since the USB port to connect to a PC is inside the camera (located under the battery compartment door). It’s done that way to maintain a water-tight shell, but is also means it can be hard to get to easily.

What has not been improved, and actually has slipped a bit, is the overall user interface (e.g., the buttons on the back). They continue to be small, hard to read, and don’t provide solid feedback that they have been pressed. Given that the camera is designed to be used in “rugged” conditions, larger buttons would have been a big plus, especially for zoom and the main menu keypad since those are used so often. Using the menu buttons is hard enough with bare hands; it’s impossible if you have gloves on.

I would certainly recommend this camera if you’re looking for a rugged point and shoot for outdoor use, but also if you’re looking for a high feature camera that never leaves the house. The performance and feature set are both excellent. The user interface brings my rating to four stars but performance and option-wise, this camera offers a lot for the price point.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-TS6A LUMIX WiFi Enabled Tough Adventure Camera (Blue)

Polaroid Cube HD 1080p Lifestyle Action Video Camera (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer] I was rather surprised when I got this with how small it is. I knew from the product description that it would be a little guy, but didn't have an appreciation for how small it was until I got it. It's a cube that is less than 1.5 inches on each side. Very compact, but it feels very solid and well-made.

Despite the compact size this is a solid performer. The video quality is quite clear and vivid provided you keep the cam steady. That's not easy to do if this is handheld given the small size, but it's designed to be mounted (there's a magnet in the base plus there are a variety of options available for mounting. Note that the mounts are sold separately).

The sound quality is good. Not spectacular, but reasonably clear and on a par with most cams I've used that have an internal mic.

Getting to the SD card is where the small size does cause a problem - it's not all that easy if you don't have nimble fingers (which I do not). You need to open the access door (which is sealed for water resistance) with a coin.

It doesn't have a lot of features which I find to be a plus since it greatly simplifies operation - the interface is a single button that turns it on/off, takes a still or starts/stops video recording. Can't get easier than that!

Minor quibbles aside, this is a solid performer and one that's well worth considering if you're looking for a very unobtrusive cam that's easy to operate (other than getting the SD card in and out). 4.5 stars rounded up to 5 due to the performance at this price point.

text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube HD 1080p Lifestyle Action Video Camera (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer]

text_fidelity_a:
HUION Inspiroy H1060P Graphics Drawing Tablet with 8192 Pressure Sensitivity Battery-Free Stylus and 12 Customized Hot Keys, 10 x 6.25 inches Digital Art Tablet for Mac, Windows PC and Android *UPDATED*
After a year of use. The tablet canvas started chipping in the middle of the protective coating. Stylus pressure and positioning still work but it's annoying as heck plus not it's even chipping more every time I go over same spot. I've never had that happen with any of the Huion & Wacom tablets I've owned for more years than this. I also can't seem to find a tablet protector for this either. So kind of bummed because I really like this...or want to really like this tablet.

*Original review*
First off, just like Wacoms these Huions are compatible with literally all major art software programs as well as budget programs.
I personally have used this Huion with Photoshop, Illustrator, 3D Studio Max, Zbrush, Mudbox, 3D Coat, Substance Painter, Clip Art Studio (Manga Studio), Krita, Painter, Paint Too Sai....can't remember the rest.
This NEW HUION 1060 PLUS is ASIN# B01FTE9HS2 and it comes with a stylus holder, 4 stylus nibs, a carrying case and drawing glove.
There is also another NEW version I saw on Amazon which includes 10 stylus nibs, holder and a glove without carrying case but they are the same exact tablet. They are both the same price on Amazon as of this writing.
Not to get you confused but there is an older one also called the 1060 Plus but it is not labled NEW or UPGRADED.
It is different cosmetically and has older technology and features.
The NEW 1060 Plus has Full-Area Surface Cover and Thinner Border, which makes the drawing surface bigger plus an attached side holder for stylus. Also, Quieter Express Keys, Better Linearity in art programs, Better pen pressure sensitivity.
(Specifications: Resolution: 5080 LPI, Report Rate: 233 RPS, 2048 Levels of Pressure, 10" x 6.25" active area.)
*Note: I just found out they released an even newer one with smoother pressure/linearity and has 8192 levels of pressure but it costs a little bit more.*

Now to the good stuff. Drivers were easy to install and worked right away; which is surprising because I've had driver issues with every non-Wacom tablets in the past. Actually, there are rare hiccups where the USB wouldn't recognize the tablet so I just have to replug back in. I've even had that issue with wacoms so I would just have to reconnect the USB back in to get it to recognize. Another common issue with older tablets (even Wacom) is that with Photoshop sometimes doesn't register the pressure sensitivity so I would have to either restart Photoshop or reconnect the USB.
But other than the super rare hiccups, this tablet looks very professional and is an great upgrade from the Huion H610 Pro, which I own, plus the Huion GT 220 graphics tablet which similar to the Wacom 22HD but way better IPS picture quality. I own the Wacom 22HD Touch and is totally not worth the $2000 I spent compared to the $700 I bought the Huion GT220 for. The Huion GT220 may have not come with express keys but I never use those awkward positioned keys anyways. I prefer the keyboard or game pad. I also owned a Wacom Intuos 2, Wacom Intuos 4 and an Intuos 4 Wireless which I've used throughout my professional career as an artist. (I wanted to compare them to see if a lower cost alternative is worth the savings). But my recommendation is if you are already an artist or aspiring to be an artist, don't hesitate on getting the tablet that gives you the best bang for your buck. Wacom does have good build but drivers can be flakey too. I've had some Wacoms stop recognizing the drivers to the point where I have to reinstall it.
With the 1060 PLUS you're pretty much set with a drawing tablet if you can't afford a Wacom or Surface Pro for all your 3D, drawing and painting needs. And to me, the pressure curve and sensitivity is feels equal to, if not better than, the Wacom tablets.

This Huion is the best bang for you buck for aspiring artist that want a professional tablet at the best price. I don't want to stray anyone away from a Wacom if they can afford it. But it's great to know that you can now save 1/5 the cost of a Wacom with the similar, if not better, specifications.
Actually, I purchased 5 of these for us artists at work and also had to recently recommend this Huion to my friends and family looking for a tablet for their kids that are also aspiring artist and animators. They showed me their kids' drawings and animation with the mouse I convinced their parents to get a drawing tablet. It is a must have for artists but you don't need to spend an arm and a leg. I truly believe this is the best $80 price range tablet on the market today that runs on Windows 10 (as of this writing). It has worked well for me for my professional (and personal) work with 3D sculpting, drawing and painting. Sorry Wacom....$250 to $300 for a comparable mid-size tablet is not aspiring artist friendly. They may look a bit cooler but they all achieve the same end. They also have Wacom Bamboos or budget Wacoms under $70 but they all lack the pressure sensitivity and features with only 1024 levels of sensitivity. I'm not a Huion salesman but this just makes sense and achieves the same end.....which is quality art without frustrating hardware and features.
text_fidelity_b: HUION Inspiroy H1060P Graphics Drawing Tablet with 8192 Pressure Sensitivity Battery-Free Stylus and 12 Customized Hot Keys, 10 x 6.25 inches Digital Art Tablet for Mac, Windows PC and Android

Bose needs to fix this outdated ridiculous low quality crap.

The output for the USB ports is 5V, 3A Max.

The USB ports glow blue whether you use them or not. The blue light is bright during the day and night, and can be seen even when there is a cable plugged into a port. I like the small size, it’s great for keeping in your bag in case you need a bunch of outlets. But it’s also functional at home, and has replaced one of my bulky power strips.

Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black The only previous experience I have had with Alexa is on my Kindle, primarily getting weather reports, etc. It took a bit of time to get it set up but once we got going my family has been enjoying it, and learning new features as we go along. So far we have been quite pleased with the wide variety of music available for free, and are impressed with the sound quality. I also made use of Alexa as a timer while I was preparing holiday meals, and just discovered that Alexa can tell me what movies are being shown nearby.

It is going to take awhile for me to explore all that Alexa is capable of doing but so far I am quite pleased with how intuitive the commands are and how responsive the programing is.

UPDATE: In the month or so that I have been using this device I continue to be impressed with the great sound this compact unit has. I can ask Alexa to play a specific genre or artist and she will shuffle through the appropriate selections in her library and then play until told to stop or her program is complete. I also enjoy getting a customized weather report on command as well as the interesting daily factoid Alexa delivers each morning in response to my greeting.

There are a couple of glitches though that have come up. The first is that Alexa will occasionally announce that she is having trouble with the wifi connection. Usually she can resolve this herself, but once in awhile the reset button needs to be used which resolves the problem in less than a minute. The other problem is rather funny. I happen to have my unit in the same room as the TV and whenever a commercial for Amazon Echo comes on my unit will respond to the 'Alexa' prompts which my family finds amusing.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth) Had a STR-DN1040, which we liked. Had no problem getting it up and running in our dedicated home theater. It worked well and sounded great. However, after 8 months the HDMI board went out (common problem we've learned). It was still under warranty, so we sent it off to Sony. Sony was not going to have the parts available for more than a month, so they offered us a brand new STR-DN1050. Sony customer service was excellent and it's hard to knock them when they offer a brand new amp that is the next newer model. We only received the new amp this week, but so far we love it. It was easy to set up and get running. I like the on screen setup display for the amp. It was very easy to navigate through. I know that several reviews I read complained about their being fewer HDMI inputs than the 1040. To us that did not matter as it is in a dedicated media room that only has a Blu-ray, DirecTV, and an iPhone connected to it. It sill has the front HDMI in the event we want to make an impromptu addition, as well more rear HDMI inputs available. I also read about folks complaining that the remote controls less functions. I am content with the new remote, as I didn't really control everything from the stock remote anyway. We really like that when we turn up the volume on the new remote, a volume control is displayed on the video screen. The 1040 did not do that and we missed it since our previous Onkyo did. There were also some concerns that the AMP was not truly 4K compatible. We use an Epson 8350 1080p projector (http://www.amazon.com/Epson-PowerLite-Home-Cinema-Projector/dp/B0044UHJWY/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1426790549&sr=8-1&keywords=Epson+8350), so not having full 4K compatibility is not a problem. To us the Blu-ray and DirecTV HD programs look awesome.

For a mid-range/price I would absolutely recommend this amp. Of course you can spend more, but why? Since the last amp went out after 8 mos, I am going to leave this review with 4 stars until we get some time under it's belt.

If you want to make your life and set up so much easier, also get the Deadbolt Banana Plugs, 12-pair, By Sewell Direct: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B006U3O566/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1
text_fidelity_b: Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth)

text_fidelity_a:
IDEALROYAL Smart Watch, Fitness Tracker for Android Phones, Smartwatch with Heart Rate,Sleep Monitor,Activity Tracker with IP67 Waterproof Pedometer Watch for Android & iOS for Men Women At time of writing, this is going for $30, but I think it may have been $20 previously. I was surprised to see those prices, because it seems pretty sophisticated. I don't have an Apple watch, but I don't imagine it does much more than this (although I could definitely be wrong). It's a shame that wearing a watch sort of irritates me because I can see a real point to having this, surprisingly.

I think the Apple watch may have wireless charging, whereas this uses a magnetic cable with a USB port on one end. This can be just a little tricky to ensure it's charging while on its side (I guess face down is fine, but then you can't be 100% certain it's actually charging), but you get the hang of it quickly.

You get a surprising amount of information on the small face, and then a few scrolls in whichever direction can give you more information. You get use to that very quickly, too, and it is, in fact, very intuitive. You can always find what you want before too long.

The main face can be flash updated, meaning you can download different themes to the device. There's a couple neat ones, but nothing too exciting. I'm guessing there may be user uploaded versions for the Apple version (or maybe not, as Apple always locks its stuff down too much), and that could happen here, too, but I'm guessing not as many people have this, which will lessen the available "content".

The step count is the main thing, along with the time. The watch usually pops on for you to see it when you raise it to look at it, but not always. Usually a shake will turn it on if it doesn't notice you raise your arm. If nothing else, you can press the button. It's a fine line, because too many false positives would also be annoying.

It seems to last a very long time, like many days. And the battery indicator has five segments instead of the three that some devices have, so you get a better indication of when you'll have to charge it.

I'm not really convinced it's super accurate with my steps, but I'm not sure the Apple version would be either. And then it makes a guess on your calorie burn based on steps, which is just for fun as far as I'm concerned. It can do a bunch of other stuff if you hook it up with your "health" app, but I never bothered setting up that app in the first place.

Other convenience factors include it vibrating when you get a call or text, which can help you notice calls and texts, especially if you have your phone on vibrate all the time like I do (and for that reason miss a lot of calls). You can also read your text messages on here, although not really so well that you wouldn't just pull your phone out of your pocket if you actually want to read it (although knowing if you can ignore it can be helpful). You can also control your music to some degree and tell your camera to take a picture, which will be wonderful if you're one of those people always taking pictures of themselves (of if you just want a picture of you and your friends without having to have someone stay behind to press the button).

It also has a timer. Some of these things require the app to be running on your phone (I'm not saying which ones for sure because I think the manual said the camera shutter wouldn't work without the app, but it does). And there is a "find phone" feature which I can't figure out how to get to work, although I haven't tried much. I mean, it's bluetooth, so if the phone is far away, it won't help you anyway.

The watch and the band look just like the Apple version from what I can tell. The band also comes off easily, so I'm assuming it can be replaced with anything that fits the Apple version, but double-check before you count on it.

Overall, I like it a lot. I'd never consider the Apple version, which I assume costs hundreds, but for a fraction of that, I think it's a pretty cool toy.
text_fidelity_b: IDEALROYAL Smart Watch, Fitness Tracker for Android Phones, Smartwatch with Heart Rate,Sleep Monitor,Activity Tracker with IP67 Waterproof Pedometer Watch for Android & iOS for Men Women

I'm not sure why this had a lot of flickering when used with my Alienware computer, but it worked perfectly with another computer and my QNAP NAS (worth noting is the NAS puts out a very weak signal and does not work with my in-place 25-ft. traditional HDMI cable).

I had almost written this off because usually HDMI is a crapshoot when it comes to any sort of distance and I didn't even realize such a product existed until I read about fiber optic cable inside. I thought that was a generic brand typo type of situation until I looked this up and realized this is a real thing. I didn't study it, but I gather/assume that there is a chip inside that changes electrical signals to low power lasers to send the signals this way. Interesting, though, because there are not 19 fibers inside (a traditional HDMI cable has 19 pins, I think).

I probably need to research this further just because it's totally cool, but I love this thing because I can now watch my NAS directly on my TV even though it is down in the basement (and there is a great app to act as a remote since I now do not have line of sight for the IR remote). I only took off a star because it apparently has some issues with my one computer - not sure why but if you need a couple of these, you might want to buy one at a time to be sure what it does and does not work with. I love it, but had to remove a star for that reason.

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500) Compared to the Crucial 1TB M2 NVME I reviewed earlier, this Sabrent 512GB model benchmarks a little faster. And it works just fine on a PCI M2 adapter card, which are only a few bucks. (I bought the cheapest one available and it works.)

The NVME still offers much faster R/W speeds than other drives even when used with SATA 1 (as on my workstation). For example, the SSD I was using as my hard disk benchmarks at about 220MB/second. The Sabrent NVME on a PCI card benchmarks at about 1.5GB/second.

This time I experimented to see if I could get Debian Linux distro running on the NVME on my older workstation.

It took a few tries. Getting the OS to boot directly from the NVME was a no-go. Since the NVME is mounted on an adapter card, I had hoped it would trick the system into thinking it was just an ordinary SATA drive and boot from it. But that didn't happen.

So what I did was installed all the Linux OS EXCEPT for the boot folder on the NVME, and put the boot folder on the SSD HDD. So it boots from the SSD but the entire OS is on the NVME and runs from it.

Step one:

The partition manager in the Debian installer didn't want to partition the NVME at first.

So I bailed out of it and used GParted (Gnome disks utility couldn't do this) to "create partition table" and selected msdos as type. That wiped everything and turned the whole drive into unallocated space. From that point the partition manager worked.

Step two:

From the linux bootable USB installer I partitioned the SSD (not the NVME) with a primary partition labeled (to be mounted) as /boot. (You can make this partition most any size from a few GB on up---the boot files don't require a lot of space.) The remaining space I manually labeled as /msc.

I partitioned the NVME so the installer would put everything else on it, starting with / (root). You can simply make the whole NVME / root and the installer will take care of putting everything else on that drive, or you can do what I did and set up size-defined partitions for /home, /usr, and so on.

After installing the system, the installer asks where you want the bootloader GRUB installed. I selected the SSD.

It worked. The SSD does the booting to the NVME, which then runs the OS. And it did improve speed.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500)

text_fidelity_a:
Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD) At first glance, this appears to be an elegant folio cover for tablets; it has an authentic-looking antique book design with embossing on the faux leather, some "gold" leafing, and real top-stitching, and it fits nicely on a book shelf (great disguise if you think you need to hide your device for whatever reason). While the design is lovely and the black microfiber supposedly prevents your screen from getting scratched, the way the tablet is held in is by four elastic straps that do an ok job, but I feel in time will wear out. Because of that concern, the design gets 4/5 stars

The function of this folio is to give the tablet a different look and ease of portability without fear of it breaking. It also helps serve as a dust cover for those who have tablets that don't always use them. This is not made for all terrain, though it's good and light weight enough for public transport. Parks and other minor recreational places are ok. I wouldn't take this folio camping or to the beach do to fear of destroying both the folio and tablet. Even though there is a cover there is a minor opening that doesn't really stay closed with the tablet in it. This folio doesn't really appear to protect a tablet from accidental drops. For every day use, this gets a 3.5/5, and for not-so every day use (rougher environments), it's closer to 1/5, so bear that in mind when deciding what case to buy.

The positive thing about this folio is that it fits most 7.1 inch tablets It did fit the Galaxy Tab 7.1 and the original kindle with keyboard. I would recommend an accessories pack to go along with the folio, since screen protector is a must! Over all for a folio I would give it 3.5/5 rounded up to 4. While is is beautiful, it only keeps to the basics of what a tablet user needs.
text_fidelity_b: Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD)

If you position the Touchpad correctly the on/off button works fine, and the volume button sort of works (can lower the volume easily but raising it requires a bit more effort).

Original review:
This is probably the most useful accessory I've every used for the iPad. Truly amazing in how it can be folded and unfolded to provide ease of use regardless of how you're using the iPad.

All the options make for a bit of a learning curve, however. I tried to follow the diagrams in the user's guide, but didn't really "get" how to use this until I watched the manufacturer's video. Highly recommend that as a guide to how to get the most out of this stand.

I'm especially pleased with being able to use it as a stand for viewing a movie (the position they call "Popcorn and a Movie" in the manual). Excellent when more than one person want to view the screen.

I can't comment with any degree of certainty as to it's longevity since I've only been using it for a few days, but it seems very sturdy. I'll update the review should that assumption prove faulty.

My big question is whether it will fit the iPad 2. Clearly it will cause problems with the cameras, but it is such a tight fit with the iPad 1 (which is a good thing in a case for security) that I'm hopeful that it will work with the iPad 2 with (perhaps) a bit of padding to make up for the thinner profile. I'll update with my experiences with the iPad 2 later this month once I have one in hand.

But regardless of fitting other models, this is an outstanding accessory for the iPad 1. Highly recommend.

Samsung Electronics UN55MU6300 55-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2017 Model) I use this as a computer monitor for my photo workstation. I use it to preview images in a catalog. At the distance used there is light fall off in the corners, so if you have the funds a curved monitor might work better for the same purpose. For my needs it is not perfect but good enough for a professional adobe display. According to my calibrator this does Adobe 87%. The IPS display it replaced was slightly higher % wise but had an annoying red color cast that I could not calibrate out.

Out of the box I got 4:2:0, I needed to get an NVIDIA 10 series card to do full 4:4:4. This did nothing for color space but did remove annoying purple "frigging" around text. You NEED a card that can do HDMI 1.4 out in order to use this as a computer monitor at 4K. In which case a NVIDIA 10 Series or AMD equivalent.

As a TV it is perfect. The low end reach of the speakers was surprising, I was going to get pc speakers but the one built in are good enough. The included apps work fine.

My only issue is the standby nag screen. If you have the TV on and turn the computer off, the TV might go in to "No signal" screen which does not seem to go away. I had the input set to PC, it should know to turn itself off. You need the remote to change the sound and turn the monitor on and off.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Electronics UN55MU6300 55-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2017 Model)

The bands are about the same size as an average rubber band or ponytail, but they have less stretch. Which makes it hard to get the bands tight around a thicker cable, like an HDMI cable.

I wouldn’t recommend using these bands for ponytails unless you’re in a pinch, or have thin hair that needs the grip of silicone. My hair is thick, so these pull at my hair. The silicone also picks up loose hair and dust, so I’ll be sticking to using them for cables.

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black

text_fidelity_a:
KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black) Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome
text_fidelity_b: KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
RayHom 8 Bay AA AAA Battery Charger, Double Charging Speed with LCD Display Independent Slot for Ni-MH AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries This is a nice alternative to chargers that require you to charge batteries in pairs. There are spaces for eight batteries, and you can charge any number within them, and mix and match AA and AAA. The eight spaces are divided electrically into two banks of four spaces, and the manufacturer says each bank can provide 2000 mA of charging power (which lowers as you add more batteries and the current is divided between them). However, the included adapter only provides only 1200 mA (so says its label), so I'm not sure the math checks out.

I gave it a test with an assortment of different brand and capacity rechargeables, then checked the batteries with a multimeter. Even fully loaded the charger worked pretty quickly and brought each one up to just over 1.4 volts. I have a brand-name charger that will bring them up to 1.5 volts, but that may be overcharging a bit and might reduce overall battery life.

The one minor negative is that the battery icons on the backlit display are pretty much invisible unless you bend down or tilt the charger up to see them. You can see how low the angle is in the photo I uploaded.

Other than that, convenient and reasonably fast, it's a nice charger.
text_fidelity_b: RayHom 8 Bay AA AAA Battery Charger, Double Charging Speed with LCD Display Independent Slot for Ni-MH AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic SC-BTT195 Energy Star 5.1-Channel 1000-Watt Full HD 3D Blu-Ray Home Theater System with Tall Boy Speakers Good sound for the money and does what I expected. Skip to the summation if you are looking for reasons not to purchase.

Might be a better choice especially if you own a Panasonic TV as the set up is designed for a Panasonic product line. I had to use their support call service a few times and as most companies today, some are very good and can understand and help, but most will read a prewritten script and hope they hit on the problem you are experiencing. Cons: Had to go buy after market speaker wires due to the lack of length that comes with the system and splice the wires to place the rear speakers. Also had to buy an audio connector to allow the system to produce TV sound. This really ticked me off and Panasonic should really step up and correct these issues. The system also needs to modernize and add another HDMI connection ( and the cable ...really? ) to allow for a cleaner install. Another con is the system will not produce sound while watching the Internet based VUDU movie channel. Panasonic wanted me to buy another movie and call them to "try" some fixes while the movie played! It does work with my cable provided paid movie service. The system would also not work with my top of the line wireless router and had to buy a cable and run wires to their system. One must also buy another adapter ( Dingle) to receive wireless signals that may or may not work or a connecting cable. Check to see see the distance from your router to the system and if it is physically possible to fish the wire to the sound system from the router before you buy the cable.

Summation: "You get what you pay for". If you can splice wires and figure out how to add cables to make TV audio work and the internet work then it's ok. You will need to spend more money on items that should be included from Panasonic and it is best to own a newer Panasonic TV for easier installation. Panasonic kind of ruined what should be a great experience by cutting corners to save money on wire and connections. Panasonic should provide more installation on information "needs" as part of their product description if they aren't not going to provide long enough speaker wire, HDMI connectors and inputs,or audio cables,or internet Dingle or cable.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic SC-BTT195 Energy Star 5.1-Channel 1000-Watt Full HD 3D Blu-Ray Home Theater System with Tall Boy Speakers

Echo Show 8 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone I purchased this for two reasons: a convenient way to display recipes that didn't require my phone being out, and streaming movies for when I'm in the kitchen for hours at a time.

I rely heavily on streaming during the holiday seasons while I bake to fulfill orders, and while the video quality was good, and the sound was AMAZING, the rest of the device was too troublesome to be worth it.
Example: Open amazon video, and it gives you 4 categories to go through, or your library. I go to my library (severe lag every single time) and I find the movie I want. I hit play, severe lag again, and it plays. Quality is not bad at all, especially for the price, but heaven forbid you have to pause. Once you pause for ~2-3 minutes, it goes to a screen saver. And when you unlock it, you have to go through the process of finding the movie all over again. It's a pain in the butt. They could at least have a "continue watching..." at the beginning of the prime menu, but it doesn't.

Secondly, our household has 3 users on our hulu account--if there was a way to switch users through the Echo, I didn't see it. I googled it, thinking I was overlooking it, and nothing. We all have very different tastes for shows/movies, and never use each others accounts for this reason. To have not one, but two streaming services being out of the question/too inconvenient to use, I couldn't handle it.

The integration was wonky at best. I have an echo dot that resides on a window sill about 3 feet from where I had my echo. My echo was off for voice recognition, but when I'd talk to my dot, it would display on my echo. This was cool except for two things: 1. It did it intermittently. 1 out of 3 times it would mirror to the echo. 2. if you were streaming something when the echo mirrored what the dot was telling you, guess what, YOU HAVE TO FIND THE MOVIE AGAIN. It was a nightmare.

Maybe down the road they'll figure out a more user friendly programming for this, but until then I'm returning it. It was meant to be a gift for family, but if I, an electronic savvy 30-something, can't figure it out, I wouldn't be comfortable giving it to my grandparents, which was the end goal.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show 8 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone

[Upgraded Version] Anker USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 10-Port Hub Including a BC 1.2 Charging Port with 60W (12V / 5A) Power Adapter [VIA VL812-B2 Chipset and Updated Firmware 9081] AH231 After having to practically rip the box to get this thing open, I set it up with my computer. The plug into the transformer is a little tight and I'm not sure it is entirely in. Though it's not moving. The computer did not recognize it at first. I do have a Sabrent 7 port hub plugged in to another USB slot on my laptop, but that is mostly filled with devices that are required for license verification (ilok, etc...) and it will only really take a powered hard drive even though it is powered.

Back to the Anker. I plugged in 2 Seagate 2 TB drives and a WD 2 TB drive, all bus powered. Once the computer finally recognized the Anker (I had to take the USB out and plug it back in) All three drives were quickly recognized. However after about 10 minutes I got a message that the last USB device I plugged in wasn't working and then the drives reconnected, except the WD This is the same behavior I was getting with my Sabrent that caused me to look for another hub. I was able to reconnect the WD by unplugging it a replugging it in. It is getting to be a very frustrating thing trying to find a USB 3.0 hub that can handle multiple drives.

I am running Windows 8 on an HP laptop. I will try this for a bit. I hope it doesn't have to go back because I had to damage the packaging to open it.

Update 12/2/16 - I've had this for 2 years. for the last year it has been a pain to use. The plug that was difficult to plug in now won't stay in. It turns off if I slightly move it. I'm looking for another one. Most of the spots are taken up by USB licensers, so when it stops working, it crashes my programs. very frustrating.
Updated 1/6/15: After keeping this plugged in, it is now working okay. I am not sure that some of the problems are not caused by my HP shutting the USB ports down as a power saver. I transferred a number of files from the WD to the Seagate using the Anker with no issues. It was actually very quick. However, I only had the 2 drives attached. I'm not sure there is anything out there that is any better. This is my 4th USB 3.0 hub I've tried and none of them really work well. And it could be my computer. But the whole point of a powered hub is that the computer doesn't have to support it.

7/16/16 Update
Still using this, but the plug doesn't like to stay in. I have to be very careful not to knock it out. Otherwise, it is still working well.
text_fidelity_b: [Upgraded Version] Anker USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 10-Port Hub Including a BC 1.2 Charging Port with 60W (12V / 5A) Power Adapter [VIA VL812-B2 Chipset and Updated Firmware 9081] AH231

This is why it is so astonishing that I have grown to love my kindle 2.

I learned how to use it easily within a few minutes. It is so intuitive- my four year old enjoys it and can page back and forth reading classics such as George MacDonald's The Princess and The Goblin or Mary Pope Osborne's The Magic Treehouse. My tween age son uses it for Shakespeare- I downloaded the First Folio (35 plays from the Bard) for all of 99 cents! It's quite a favorite amongst my children and I have recently learned that if more than one family member has a kindle, all e-books may be shared with a single purchase. My friend can even access her kindle books and magazines from her iphone!

Cool features include 6 different options for font size, and text markers by "location" to bring you to the same line of text whether you use the biggest or smallest of fonts, as page numbers would vary too much to be useful. A male or female voice can read to you, though the voices are a bit stiff and robotic, and they make small mistakes such as using alternate pronunciation that don't fit context with heteronyms such as read/read or live/live. You can connect speakers or earbuds/headphones for this feature. Magazines can be downloaded as a single issue or a subscription, but the subscriptions cannot be canceled from the kindle- the user must go to amazon's "Manage my kindle" area to do this.

I have downloaded quite a few classic books for free and spent about a dollar on many others. So far, the younger children's literature has been somewhat limited, but I imagine that as prices drop, more will become available. I am a bibliophile and I never thought I would love a paper book replacement, but this device is so clean and glare free that I forget I am not looking at a paper page.

I'm sure that color kindles will be available within a few years, to make the illustrations a bit more interesting. I love the beautiful pen and ink type renderings which fill the kindle 2 screen when it isn't in use. Obviously though, color would be more attractive with other types of art. Black and white is easiest on the eyes for text, and mostly that it what kindle is all about.

The kindle 2 holds a charge for a long time. I think I plug mine in about once every couple of weeks. If you are not careful with the five way button, sometimes you do end up getting the wrong result. I purchased a book accidentally this way, but amazon has a handy "did you purchase this by mistake?" option which permits you to cancel the order if you act right away.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless)

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Once calibrated, this PC tablet works wonderfully. It is responsive to the stowable stylus or a tap of my fingernail, and I can even scroll with my thumb after adjusting the right edge width. The screen is sharp and clear, and it's speedy enough for pleasurable surfing and blog-reading, which is what I mostly want to use it for. I have not watched any HD movies on it yet, although the sample movie clip included with the computer shows what it's capable of...and it's gorgeous.

But I have a problem with the Archos 9. Because there is no fan, which makes for a very quiet experience, the lithium battery does get hot when held in your hands. Now, maybe there are people who will use this computer by pulling out the little easel-like stick in the back, but not me. I want to curl up on the sofa with it like a book. So I could see immediately that I wanted to rotate my Archos 9 PC Tablet's screen to portrait orientation so the battery would be at the top and not bother me so much. Well, doing so was a BIG mistake. Once you rotate the screen, it's pretty much impossible to recalibrate it; trying to move the cursor is like trying to walk without an inner ear: Directions ceased to make sense and I'd skew off East (or was it West?) when I meant to move North. It was all I could do to manage to restore the computer to its earlier state.

The little end piece of the easel-like appendage pulled off and I had to super-glue it back on, but that wasn't such a big deal. This appendage also stows into the back of the computer, and it can be pulled out short or long depending on whether you are watching a movie or trying to type on the on-screen keyboard. I can see it for watching a movie, but there's no way I'd ever try to type on the on-screen keyboard. Hunt-and-peck with the stylus is quicker. Needless to say, I will reach for my laptop if I have to do much typing.

I installed Skype, but it was too slow to show video unless I stopped everything else from running. This is fine with me, however, because I prefer to use Skype without the visuals. Google Chrome runs very well on it. I found I preferred the software keyboard (which you can drag around the screen) to the one that pops up when you press the keyboard key. I found that by keeping the former loaded and minimized to the tray, I can get around and do things online pretty efficiently. I just wish that battery didn't get so hot OR that I could easily/reliably rotate the screen to portrait. I gave this computer four stars because, on the whole, it's quite nice. But I must say that I am not likely to reach for the Archos 9 very often because of the discomfort from the battery heat when holding it in my hands. If they will come out with a software upgrade that will make screen rotation practical, then I will be a lot happier with this tablet PC.

A word to the wise: Immediately when you take your Archos 9 out of the box and get the software installed, you need to back it up. Don't wait a second longer than you have to. I was able to restore mine to its pristine newly installed state, but had I not backed it up, the whole thing would have been trashed by my little screen rotation exploit. You don't have a restore disk with this product. So be careful.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

The interesting thing is that I'm not even interested in the bluetooth capability. I want the aux connection for my first generation iPod, which doesn't have bluetooth technology. My iPhone just doesn't have the space for all the music I have on the iPod, plus I don't want to use up data streaming Pandora. Additionally, bluetooth and getting stuff to connect is just a pain. So, I've never tried to connect via bluetooth only the aux.

At first I thought I had dud. I charged it and went to push the power button and nothing happened. I read the tiny print in the instructions and still nothing. So, I went on YouTube to see if anyone made video about using this and of course there is! So, you have to press the power button until the device glows blue and beeps! No where on the instructions does it say to do this! So, once you do this, then you can follow the directions to use the speaker. If you are going to just use the aux plug then push the "M" button, which I think stands for mode. You're good to go.

Now this is tiny, so you're going to get a lot of output, but it what it does put out is a decent sound. I have used mine in a small pavilion for a party and on my front porch. At the party depending on the song, a few downloaded from the early aughts were too quiet to hear, but songs downloaded from iTunes or from CDs came out loud enough to hear throughout the pavilion. Just make sure the volume is up on your speaker AND your device. I've used for about 12 hours total. 4 hours here, 4 hours there, etc., and I still haven't charged it. So it holds a good charge to last through a party or an afternoon lounging on the porch.

You get an aux cord and a USB charging cord. So you can charge it on the computer or with a charger plug that uses a USB plug. The light ring turns red when charging and goes off when it's fully charged. The ring glows blue when it is on. It flashes when it it searching or looking for a bluetooth device. HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder I am impressed right off the bat with just how many useful accessories are included right off the bat. The description says it does not come with an SD card or AAA batteries, but mine did, perhaps for review purposes, although the box did not look like it had been opened. Seems like it would come with that stuff, so perhaps other reviewers might clarify. There is a case and two separate pouches for the wider camera lens and the microphone.

Functionality and video quality are pretty good. I guess the only drawback is that this almost seems like a throwback now. For still pictures - on a vacation or a great hike where I want to take great pictures - I still take along a small camera instead of just my cell phone, but the truth is cell phone cameras are getting so good now that I wonder when that will no longer seem prudent. And with that said, my small camera takes such amazing (not studio quality) HD that I wonder when something like this would really seem like the best thing, especially considering they both take SD cards and length is only limited by SD card capacity.

It certainly does seem like a more professional camera in its size and shape, but mostly because that style has been the trend for some time now. But in a way this style is already starting to seem outdated, like a throwback. I also noticed, just now, that even the really big name manufacturers have this style in 1080p for comparable prices.

I'd definitely give this thing a look. I would have totally loved it a few years ago. The mic and extra lens still feel like premium features, but I'm rarely the one to set up for photos and video footage, as I usually just do landscapes or great spontaneous moments. This may be a fantastic alternative to giving kids your phone - or a phone - to play with. Seems like a good way to encourage their inner photographer without it leading into a bunch of cheap phone games.

Camera has mini* USB and HDMI ports (as opposed to micro) - just when I was wondering what I'd ever do with this one mini-HDMI cable I have... Mic takes 2xCR2032 batteries, which are included, and should probably last, as I don't think mics eat up much power. Has a curled, springy, analogue audio cable with stereo mini-plugs on both ends to connect the mic. Also has an external battery charger.

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) [[VIDEOID:c23012732deceb9d78b96d41ac89bfcb]] [[VIDEOID:56e6589f81a80deb1709b51fc87a42ef]] [[VIDEOID:bdf9b77251e219b84bed6372225dbf2a]] [[VIDEOID:838bfc2c03ad2a6d884b05f4a37eddbe]] [[VIDEOID:f7f3bb80516774e2cc828f076249211a]] [[VIDEOID:d48cd1a96b9a119e675001d320845a53]] [[VIDEOID:9363c8a20797fe64545aeb51179ca502]] [[VIDEOID:3371609d21e77efbab0cfd0f6265a782]] This is a terrific little action camera that has remarkable clear video, good audio and is extremely easy to use. I understand there were some problems with audio in the earlier versions, but it seems to be all fixed now because the sound quality was excellent when tested both indoors and outside.

I won't bore you with going over all of the specs which you can read in the product description, but I'll tell you how easy it is to use. Mine arrived partially charged, so I used my fingernail to open the back port and inset the included 8gb micro SD card, then charged it fully within an hour. On a full battery it can operate for about 107 minutes and when depleted it takes between 1.5 to 2 hrs to fully charge.

I downloaded the app to my iPad for free from the app store, then did some testing. It connected easily to my WiFi and the interface understandable and easy to use giving you the choice to shoot still photos or videos in several different resolutions. You can also import the photos or videos taken with the camera to your cell phone, your iPad, or share them using the WiFi connection to import them.

This little camera takes gorgeous high def photos, and the audio inside is crystal clear. When I was offered the opportunity by the manufacturer to test the Cube+ I went ahead and purchased a [[ASIN:B00NXK3JTI Polaroid Helmet Mount for the Polaroid CUBE, CUBE+ HD Action Lifestyle Camera]] so I would be able to properly test it in action in order to determine video and sound quality outside in the elements.

I attached the helmet mount to my 9 y/o granddaughter's helmet, placed the Cube+ in it, started it through the app on my iPad and sent her out on her scooter to see how the video and audio quality was. I've attached a short part of the video here so you can assess it for yourself, but I'm quite pleased with the quality of both the picture and the sound, and I didn't experience any lag time in regards to the app.

It does record video in MP4 format, so if you have trouble hearing the audio on your computer you should download QuickTime Player or VLC Player. Both downloads are free and should allow you to view the files and hear the audio. VLC also has a free converter available in case you prefer to use Windows Media Player or Windows Movie Maker. I use a free app called Trim & Cut on my iPad which shortens, condenses, and converts my videos to the format I prefer, and that's what I used for the video I've attached here.

This is a reasonably priced tough little action camera that's easy to use and produces great quality video. It's weather resistant and splashproof so it can handle the outdoors already, but I plan to buy the waterproof case for it so we can have fun swimming with it on this summer. I don't own a GoPro, so I have nothing to compare this to, but from a user's stand point I can definitely tell you that this is user friendly, easy to operate and does a remarkably good job! Enjoy!

This camera was provided at no cost by the manufacturer for evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers With crime rates going up in NYC, this is an ideal kit for anyone living in an apartment, especially if they're alone and elderly. It covers two areas most vulnerable to thieves: your window and the door, while the key chain is best for when you're coming home late at night on a dark, lonely street. Just pull the pin and the alarm screams.

Of the three items, I would say the window alarm rates highest in terms of usefulness. In fact, I wish this set came with three of them. We travel a lot, and the biggest fear we have is intruders breaking in through our high-rise window, as we have a fire escape near one of them.

The door stop is the least useful to me as a thief would have to break through one of our windows first before going through a door. My front door is already secured by locks and the other doors in our place generally remain open. I suppose we could reinforce the front door with the doorstop, but it seems like overkill. If you lived in a dorm and wanted a particular room to be off-limits, I suppose it would be useful in that case. This item reminds me of the alarm that would be set off if you used an emergency exit. As if in acknowledgement that this item won't be used as much as the others, no battery was supplied for it, unlike the others.

As for the key chain, this is one of those devices that will lay dormant for long periods (knock on wood). You'll have to remember to check and test the batteries occasionally because it will be rarely used.

Overall, for the price this set can't be beat. It feels more like a "sampler" pack, though, as it has only one of each product when multiples of each one would have been more helpful.

iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey Last year I switched to a Macbook Pro 13-inch after being a PC user since the early eighties. I love my Mac, but I haven't gone whole-hog for the rest of the pricey iProducts Apple puts out. Still, this case is just about perfect for my needs.

First, I like how the zippered compartment for the computer does not unzip all around. It's really easy to slip my Mac in and out of its fleecy padded pocket while still feeling like it's protected. (There's also plenty of room for my little wireless mouse dongle, although I don't use a mouse much anymore.) The iPad compartment is similar, and it holds my Kindle Fire in its rooCase with room to spare for something else (like a checkbook or wallet perhaps). The clever half-case compartment with pockets for chargers, headphones, and pens has plenty of room for my Mac power supply, Kindle charger and cables, and another charger if I need it.

The full compartment in the middle of the case is for whatever you might stick in it. It's not huge in depth, but it would certainly hold a legal pad/portfolio and a magazine or two. I don't use a cell phone now, but one day I might, so the outer pocket for the phone is nice; it's also serviceable for one of those small flashlights or perhaps a set of keys (on the right keychain). Toothbrush! I could see using the sleeve as a lapdesk/laptop stand while seated on a plane or in a doctor's office.

The sleeve comes with a classy, comfortable shoulder strap with strong, reliable clips. At first it wasn't clear what the the clips were supposed to clip to, but they are hidden away under the edges of the center gusset (what you see as the narrow black line running across the thickness in the photo here). There's no tangling up with this shoulder strap, either; the business ends can be rotated to keep the strap straight.

It's lightweight. And the color? It's a perfect match for the Mac Lion startup screen, of course. Everything about it says "Mac," including the iHome logo, but you don't have to be an Apple nut to love this sleeve. Very well designed.
text_fidelity_b: iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey

Power Strip with 3 USB, KPSTEK Flat Plug Extension Cord with 2 Widely Spaced Outlets, Desktop Charging Station for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, Black - KS2312 This is a combination product with a 5 foot extension cord, 2 AC power outlets, and 3 full-sized USB power ports. Compact size is great for travel, since older hotels don't have enough power outlets for modern travelers and the outlets are often hidden behind desks or under beds.

Unfortunately, the USB power ports are pretty weak. You get 2.4A divided among 3 ports, so if you're trying to charge 3 devices, each one gets less than 1A. Modern smartphones and tablets will often fast-charge at 3A, so charging with these ports will be very slow. USB powered laptops can use even more power and will complain about being charged at less than 3A.

I don't like that there is no USB-C charging port and no USB Power Delivery fast charging, which are becoming the standard for smartphones and laptops.

This device is not UL listed for electrical safety. As phone and tablet and laptop batteries get more and more powerful, electrical safety becomes more and more important. Most power strips from US brands are UL listed, so I cannot recommend a product that is not UL listed.
text_fidelity_b: Power Strip with 3 USB, KPSTEK Flat Plug Extension Cord with 2 Widely Spaced Outlets, Desktop Charging Station for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, Black - KS2312

My cable modem (a Motorola) and router (a Linksys) get about 60 minutes of run time off of the battery, which is more than enough for my needs.

HaoZi SLIronM-01 All-in-One Universal Travel Adapter with 3.4A 4 USB, Europe Multifunctional Power Adapter Wall Charger, Black Product looks and feels nice (smooth matte), and even like quality.

I guess, since you're really only using this for electronics with rectifiers built in, you really don't need it to be grounded. It is a shame, in that case, that the stupid UK/Middle-East plug has to have the dielectric prong instead of the ground because a lot of their outlets are tamper resistant (but that is not this product's fault).

Speaking of UK plugs and their bulk, this device isn't really all that big when you're used to carrying some UK adapters around anyway. And now you also don't really need your five volt power adapters.

You can usually force a "European plug" (this one is like an ungrounded Schuko plug) into the lower amperage (smaller) Italian socket (and you can often rest an ungrounded, lower amperage, Italian plug into a Schuko or other Euro outlet), but it is not ideal, and I actually don't want to put that kind of stress on a $20 product (whereas throwaway adapters are okay for this purpose). Italians sometimes have mainland or combo outlets in their hotels, but it would be more ideal if a proper Italian plug and outlet was included in this device yet. I mean, it's just Italy, but everyone wants to go there, and I happen to have work there, so that would make this more ideal. Truth is, I'll probably always carry various extra adapters anyway.

USB ports can do .85amps each if they're all being used, but the truth is that I have a lot of old USB chargers that only do 500mA, so everything will charge, maybe just slowly if you have them all used. But each port can do 2.4a if used individually.

Overall, it's the coolest and most inclusive such adapter that I've seen.
text_fidelity_b: HaoZi SLIronM-01 All-in-One Universal Travel Adapter with 3.4A 4 USB, Europe Multifunctional Power Adapter Wall Charger, Black
