text_fidelity_a:
Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System First, I have to say, these sound amazing for their size, picking up even most low frequencies. Crank them up, and they almost vibrate themselves off the table - you can feel the bass just by putting your hand in the open air behind them. I can say confidently that these sound better than the old Boston Acoustics computer speakers that included a small subwoofer.

They are also good looking, have a standard auxiliary input in the back for versatility, and have a headphone output in the front (still trying to figure out when that could come in handy...) They also connect easily to my BB 9700, Xoom, and Win7 PC. Surprisingly, I can even control the volume from the speakers or from the controlling device!

The one speaker has a ~1.5m cable permanently attached that ends in an RCA plug that must be plugged into the other speaker. That can be extended, of course, but somehow, this makes the whole wireless thing less impressive. Somehow, I'd like to have them both pick up Bluetooth separately, but then of course, both would need separate power supplies and receptacles. The point is, for installations such as a home computer setup, what is the point of going Bluetooth for speakers? On the other hand, it is super cool to be able to just spit music from your phone at any time.

My other qualm is that they should have grill covers; I tend to pick them both up with one hand and have to be a bit careful not to stick my finger through the cone.

Overall, I'm impressed with the technology and the product itself. If you have a good use for this particular type of product and can deal without grill covers, I'm sure you'll be happy with the purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System

Jabra Stealth Bluetooth Headset - Black (US Version) I am pleased with this headset; the sound quality is good and audibility is very sharp. The music quality is also good. Assembly is very simple and needs no additional tools to set it together. It also fits well into my ears. I have been using this set for the last three weeks and it works great. It is paired with my cell phone and I use this to listen to the incoming calls and also listen to the music from micro SD card inserted into the cell phone. It is small and has a discreet design. It is very light, easy to carry and works great. The gadget also synchronizes easily with phone, but it does not pair with my Garmin Nuvi GPS machine or my Acer Chromebook both of which are Bluetooth-enabled.

Pairing with cell phone is very easy; just turn the headset on and the cell phone on, it detects the Bluetooth easily and within a minute it gives the message that it is paired. The built-in battery is excellent, and on one charge it lasts for about 5-6 hours of use time. The downside is that this piece doesn't have a separate mute button or the volume button; you have to control volume from your cell phone. Another negative feature is that the three replacement parts for earpiece that comes with the set are of same size, hence gives little option for someone with small (or large) ears. I have rated this product four stars for overall satisfaction.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Stealth Bluetooth Headset - Black (US Version)

APEKX Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3: IPX7 Waterproof, Stereo Sound, Built-in Mic, Earbuds for Gym & Workouts, True Wireless Earphones (Black) I've had several different pairs of earbuds, all purchased from Amazon and none were name brands. So far, with the wrapping ear piece, this pair seems to stay on my ears much better than the buds that just pop into the ears. They paired easily to my iPhone and connect automatically each time I take them out of the case. The sound is decent or at least decent enough for me. I do not use these for just listening to music or videos, I have better over the ear headphones for that purpose. For me, I just use these for running, working out or maybe while working around the yard. For that purpose, the sound quality is pretty good. The only suggestion I have is remember to take the clear tape off the charging contacts; I did not realize it was there and my earbuds were not charging each time I put them back in the case. On the upside, I did learn that the battery life is excellent on these earbuds. I cannot say how long they actually lasted before I charged them, but I probably went on 5 or 6 runs before the first ear bud died. With the tape off the contacts, they do charge automatically each time they are placed back in their case. A nice feature is that the case can be charged either with a cord or by setting the case on a charging pad. The price was reasonable. I would recommend these wireless earbuds to anyone looking for a set. Since I cannot fully say how long they will last or how durable they are, I will reserve the 5th star until I have owned these for a while.

Updated 12May21: Ok, I really want to like earbuds, but I cannot. As many times as I have tried earbuds, they just always feel like they are coming out of my ears, even w/the ear wraps on these buds. Having to continuously re-seat the ear buds in my ears while running just doesn't make for a comfortable run. So, I went back to a pair of wired BT headphones; which sit in my ears much better.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player I've had my Sony S350 Blu-Ray player for over a year now and here are my thoughts. The picture is completely amazing, even makes regular dvd's look better. I love that there's no more cords for picture and more cords for sound, just one HDMI cable and poof - high quality picture and surround sound.

A couple things to consider before buying your Blu-Ray player and subsequent Blu-Ray discs:
1. Blu-Ray will play your regular dvd's but if you have a regular dvd player (such as in your car) you cannot play Blu-Ray discs in it.

2. Patience is needed with this unit. After putting in a movie, especially if it is somewhat new, it could take 3-5 minutes to load. I am personally never in that much of a hurry to start the movie. While the movie is loading (a progress/status bar is provided on-screen) I can make popcorn, get the dogs situated, etc.

3. In conjunction with #2, the owner of this player must also be diligent about updating the firmware inside the player. I updated my player once last year (in November) and have noticed slower loads with current movies, so I plan to update it again next month (March). My guess is that it's good to update it 1-2 times per year.
What's involved in updating the firmware? I log onto a blu-ray firmware site, choose my model of player, then burn the update to a dvd disc. Place the disc in the player, it will read and update your firmware (took mine about 5-10 minutes as I remember). Afterward, your player will load movies more quickly.
Note: Loading never occurs during the movie, the only load-time that is experienced comes immediately after inserting the disc. Here's an example of the patience it takes to operate this blu-ray player:
Turn the player on - wait about 30 seconds for the unit to be able to receive or eject a disc (if you're trying to quickly eject a disc and run it back to the movie store, this can seem long!)
Insert disc and close - wait 3-5 minutes for movie menu to load

After that, you're set to go. For me, it's worth the wait and the trouble to keep it updated. I am quite sure that future models will require less patience and diligence, but for now this is the way it is. If you want extremely good quality with your movies, it's a wonderful addition to your home theater.
text_fidelity_b: Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player

WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black I give this drive five stars for its size - its physical dimensions - because although I have the same quibbles about it as I do with all other external drives, its size is smaller than other 2.5" external hard drives I've seen, including the 1.5TB Seagate that I own.

In the 2.5" hard drive world - the drives that can run on just USB power - there are internal drives that you can pair with an external case and there are external drives that come in a case and with software - usually a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to help the layman back things up. Unlike the 3.5" hard drive world, capacities are larger earlier in the external devices, but somehow the casing and enclosed bridge (in this case SATA to USB) make the physical size larger than an internal drive with case. This one is still a little bigger, but really quite small. It's awesome, frankly. To have that much capacity in something you can store just about anywhere and you don't even have to mess around with a power cord.

What I don't like - and I complain about this with all external hard drives - is the included software that they want you to install to do backups, etc. As an advanced computer user, I think it's nonsense; even my mother should be able to use the drive without any software. Of course you don't have to use it. The thing that annoys me is that the drive - again, like all other externals nowadays - comes with a sleep timer set, in this case at 30 minutes, so I have to install the interface software to turn that off (necessary for my intended application), and then uninstall the software to get it off my system, but all software leaves a trace after its removal.

If this is your first USB 3.0 peripheral, be aware that the port on the drive is unlike any USB 2.0 port, and thus will require a different cable if you need one longer than the included ~1m cable. More industry stupidity, so they can overcharge for the first year or so. Look for a cheap one on Amazon so you don't have to run out to Best Buy and pay 10x too much. Interface cables are the one thing I believe in buying as cheap as possible - and thank God for Amazon in that respect.

One more note in response to another review: prices on non-solid state hard drives have been fluctuating a lot recently because of the Thai floods, and prices of electronics on Amazon always fluctuate. I typically check all prices before buying anything, but still end up buying from Amazon 99% of the time. I haven't seen Best Buy have a real deal in years. They make their money off lies that their employees tell you, either because they have been brainwashed in to believing said lies or because of commission. Do your own price comparison when the time comes to make a purchase.

The only thing I don't love about this drive is an industry problem that's not going away any time soon, and I have to just stop complaining about it (later). I give this a higher than average review because I was actually surprised - and impressed - with the physical size.
text_fidelity_b: WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green) I'm not going to bother with a detailed listing of times as many other reviewers have done a nice job with that. I'll just say that I did time out this device in comparison to a pair of my 2.0 flashdrives and another 3.0 on a pair of Macs, one with 2.0 USB and one with 3.0 USB. There's no doubt it's speedier in all cases than my 2.0s, whether I was transferring over a folder with a lot of docs or a folder with mixed media (docs, photos, video). Roughly 2-3 times as fast than 2.0 consistently (that's with both of them in the 2.0 ports), though the gap narrowed with really large, mixed folders. When it goes into the 3.0, it was consistently 3-4 times faster, with again a narrower gap with really large, mixed files. In comparison to a Triton, it was definitely significantly and noticeably slower, a little bit better than half as fast.

The device feels very light and the casing not quite as sturdy as my other drives, though I never feel like it's in danger of breaking. Just doesn't have the same sense of heft and durability.

On the other hand, the slide clicks in nicely and solid, with a satisfying sound and doesn't retract easily unless you are wanting it to

If you have a 2.0 drive, it'll be noticeably faster and if you're looking for a drive, makes sense to get one that can go with you to your next upgrade. If you've upgraded to 3.0 and want a new drive just for that, there's no doubt you'll notice the difference, and especially with large files and movies etc. I'd ay it's definitely worth it. As for going beyond to the Triton, personally my need for speed isn't that great--this one would suit me fine. Some people though have less patience than I do. Plus, I'm cheap. So slower than the other 3.0, but I'd say still a fine value.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green)
